description:
ecoinvent gives every flow a code that never changes, and this project writes its corrections against that code, once, so that a correction covers every release shipping the flow. The premise is usually right and occasionally not: the same code can arrive in the next release carrying a different registry number, which is ecoinvent saying the flow is a different substance. Nine codes went from `Chromium`, 7440-47-3, in release 3.8 to `Chromium III`, 16065-83-1, in 3.9.1 and after -- and the correction written about the trivalent flow carries back to 3.8, because 3.8 shipped a separate `Chromium VI` flow in those same nine places, so its unspeciated chromium already meant everything-but-hexavalent. Thirteen codes went from `Vanadium`, 7440-62-2, and `Vanadium, ion`, 22541-77-1, to a single `Vanadium V`, 22537-31-1, and there the correction does not carry: three substances arrived under one set of codes, and #108 stopped the pentavalent decision from reaching the other two.

Same shape, opposite answers, and nothing recorded which of the twenty-two had been thought about. Measured across the five releases extracted on 2026-08-18 -- 3.8, 3.9.1, 3.10.1, 3.11 and 3.12 -- twenty-seven of the 375 corrections are about a flow ecoinvent has renumbered, five more than the two releases a build merges show: `Copper oxychloride` carries 1332-40-7 in 3.9.1 and 3.10.1 and 1332-65-6 in 3.11 and 3.12, under the same name, and nobody had looked. It carries, on the project's own record -- `curated-chebi-roles.json` cites PPDB for both numbers naming dicopper chloride trihydroxide, the copper fungicide.

What this file states is the answer the chromium correction gives, in both releases a build merges, because that is what the change must not move: a rule that made the renumbering check refuse rather than record would take the nine 3.8 rows off trivalent chromium and score them as the element. Measured on the 2026-08-18 build of `e822c1c`, merging ecoinvent 3.12 and 3.8, unbounded. See #109, #108, #49, #45.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.8's nine `Chromium` emissions reach trivalent chromium, though 3.8 registers them as the metal
expectations.comment: The half of the renumbering question that says *yes*. These nine rows carry 7440-47-3, the registry number of chromium metal, and reach trivalent chromium anyway, on a correction written about the flow 3.9.1 renamed `Chromium III`. That is right and it was checked (#45), but until now the check lived only in a paragraph of prose: the row itself said nothing, and the identical shape thirteen rows later -- vanadium -- has the opposite answer. The nine rows now record the two registry numbers the decision was checked against, so a release that registers the flow as a third one reopens it instead of inheriting the answer. Since #141 the substitution happens at data preparation -- the canonical-identities file reads 3.9.1 as the vendor correcting 3.8, and the rows are *recorded* under the canonical name the substitution matched with, `Chromium III` -- so the selector names that. Fourteen rows rather than nine: the five water rows, which 3.8 shipped as `Chromium, Ion` and the override file already sent to the same substance, carry the same canonical name now, and all fourteen land on trivalent chromium.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.12's `Chromium III` emissions reach the same substance the 3.8 rows do
expectations.comment: The release the correction was written about, stated beside the release it carries to, because the property worth checking is that the two agree. 3.12 ships the flow in fourteen contexts against 3.8's nine -- the nine the correction names, plus five water contexts every published table already sends to trivalent chromium -- and all fourteen carry 16065-83-1.

expectations.title: Copper oxychloride is published once, whichever of its two registry numbers a release states
expectations.comment: The row nobody had looked at, and the reason the count is twenty-seven rather than the twenty-two two releases show. Five corrections decline the published table's routing of this fungicide into `Fungicides, unspecified`; ecoinvent registers those five flows as 1332-40-7 in 3.9.1 and 3.10.1 and as 1332-65-6 in 3.11 and 3.12. A build merging 3.12 and 3.8 cannot see the disagreement -- 3.8 does not ship the flow at all -- which is exactly why the question is now asked of every extracted release rather than of the pair a build happens to merge. This expectation is about the substance rather than the rows because that is what the two numbers have to agree on.
